units.text: In the UK (MHRA, September 2026), Ozempic is licensed for diabetes and Mounjaro for diabetes and weight. Wegovy is licensed for weight management and cardiovascular risk reduction; MHRA added weight management to Mounjaro in November 2023. MHRA says retatrutide is not authorised in the UK and anyone selling it does so illegally (24 July 2026), and in May 2026 it made its largest seizure of unlicensed weight-loss medicines.

In the EU, semaglutide is authorised as Ozempic for diabetes (since 8 February 2018) and Wegovy for weight management (since 6 January 2022), and tirzepatide as Mounjaro for diabetes and adult weight management (since 15 September 2022), all prescription-only. In June 2024 EMA and HMA's shortage steering group said GLP-1 receptor agonists are not approved for, and should not be used for, cosmetic weight loss, and on 3 September 2025 EMA and HMA warned of a sharp rise in illegal medicines sold online and on social media as semaglutide, liraglutide or tirzepatide, which are unauthorised and may not contain the stated substance.

In Portugal, Wegovy and Mounjaro are authorised through the EU centralised procedure and are prescription-only, and on 4 July 2024 INFARMED stated that Ozempic, Trulicity and Victoza must not be prescribed to patients who are not diabetic (Circular 045/CD/100.20.200). In September 2025 INFARMED relayed the EMA and HMA warning of a sharp increase in the illegal marketing of medicines presented as GLP-1 receptor agonists, and stated that in Portugal medicines can only be bought on the internet from the websites of pharmacies and licensed non-prescription medicine outlets (LVMNSRM).

In Brazil, as of September 2026, Ozempic is indicated for adults with insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus, Wegovy is indicated for weight management in adults, Mounjaro is indicated for chronic weight management in adults, and the approved synthetic semaglutide copies are indicated for adult patients with insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus. Nota Técnica 200/2025 (August 2025) permits compounding of chemically synthesised APIs provided registered medicines with the same molecule already exist in Brazil, and ANVISA inspections from January to April 2026 led to the closure of 8 of the 26 establishments assessed and the seizure of more than 1.3 million units of irregular injectable medicines.

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) announced on 1 June 2026 that it had approved oral Wegovy (semaglutide) for long-term weight management in adults with obesity, or overweight with weight-related conditions, and a Ministry of Health and Prevention alert (Circular 9217/2024, October 2024) described genuine Mounjaro as registered for type 2 diabetes and weight management. Federal Decree-Law 38/2024 bars compounding pharmacies from compounding essential copies of products that hold an EDE marketing approval unless no commercially available product can deliver the expected benefit to the patient. On 20 July 2026 the EDE warned that 1,659 packs of Mounjaro and Ozempic missing from a warehouse are outside the legitimate supply chain and told the public to buy these medicines only from licensed pharmacies.

Human evidence
Large trials, measured on the scale.
In STEP-1, 1,961 adults without diabetes lost a mean 14.9% of body weight on semaglutide over 68 weeks, against 2.4% on placebo. In SURMOUNT-1, 2,539 adults lost 15.0% to 20.9% on tirzepatide over 72 weeks, depending on dose, against 3.1% on placebo. Both Hormonaly guides grade weight management A. Across 35 randomized trials of incretin drugs, a median of about 28% of the weight lost was muscle-related tissue.

Four registers
'Ozempic face', answer by answer.

Volume loss
Losing fat deflates the superficial facial compartments and unmasks laxity that was already there.

Observational and small: C to D
One imaging study of 20 patients found a median 9% loss of midface volume, mostly superficial, about 7% per 10 kg lost. A survey of 1,226 patients found sagging, facial volume loss and hair shedding reported more often the more weight was lost. A systematic review of the plastic-surgery literature found it limited by study bias. No randomized trial has measured the face.

What changes in practice
Counsel before, record during, refer when asked.
Raise facial volume change and hair shedding before treatment starts; the Hormonaly guide advises this especially for older patients. During treatment, photograph the face with consent, and support the protein intake and resistance training the guide recommends to protect lean mass. When a patient wants the face restored, refer to a qualified aesthetic or dermatology colleague. Published advice on restoration is expert opinion, the main consensus statement was developed with industry involvement, and randomized trials of fillers and devices in these patients are registered without results. Decisions about the medicine itself stay with the prescriber and the patient.

Lesson 3.3 · Concept
Inflammation that comes with age.
Inflammaging is the chronic, low-grade, sterile inflammation that rises with age. In older adults, higher IL-6 and CRP predict frailty and death. One proposed source is the gut. In mice, a high-fat diet raises circulating bacterial lipopolysaccharide, and infusing it reproduces weight gain and insulin resistance. In 12 healthy men, a single high-fat meal raised plasma endotoxin within four hours. Whether a leaky gut drives skin disease in people has not been shown.
Inflammaging: low-grade, sterile, age-related
Metabolic endotoxaemia: gut bacterial LPS in the blood
Gut to skin in people: not shown

The evidence
Thirty-nine trials of probiotics for eczema.
An independent Cochrane review pooled 39 randomized trials, with 2,599 participants, of oral probiotics for eczema. Probiotics probably make little or no difference to patient-rated symptoms, and investigator-rated severity fell by less than the minimum clinically important difference. A 2024 European task-force meta-analysis in children without food allergy reported a significant fall in severity scores.

Diet first, a bottle last.

units.text:
Mechanism
A plasma tripeptide with a copper habit.
GHK is a tripeptide found in human plasma, first described in 1973. Bound to copper it becomes GHK-Cu, which is proposed to deliver copper to enzymes such as superoxide dismutase and lysyl oxidase and to switch on wound-healing and antioxidant gene programmes. Most of that mechanistic literature comes from the group that discovered the peptide.
Endogenous: GHK circulates in human plasma
Proposed: copper delivery to matrix and antioxidant enzymes
Mechanism register only — written largely by the originator
Narration: Start with the molecule. GHK is a three-amino-acid peptide that circulates in human plasma; it was first described in 1973. It binds copper readily, and the copper complex, GHK-Cu, is what skin-care labels mean when they say copper peptide. The proposed mechanism is that GHK-Cu delivers copper to enzymes that build and protect…

units.text:
Human evidence
One indexed randomized trial.
A search of PubMed in September 2026 found one randomized controlled trial of topical GHK-Cu in human skin: 2006, healing after CO₂ laser resurfacing. The cosmetic trials cited for anti-ageing claims are manufacturer-sponsored and not indexed. Both Hormonaly guides grade topical use C.
1
indexed randomized trial of topical GHK-Cu in human skin
Miller et al., 2006 — healing after CO₂ laser resurfacing, not photoageing
What it means: The human evidence for topical GHK-Cu is small: one small indexed trial plus sponsor-run cosmetic studies. GRADE C is the honest ceiling.
What it does not mean: It does not show that GHK-Cu fails, that it treats photoageing, or anything about injecting it. A thin evidence base is an unknown, not a negative.

units.text: In the UK, anything injected falls outside cosmetics law, and MHRA decides whether it is a medicine from its claims, form and use. In the UK, a GHK-Cu serum presented for appearance is a cosmetic, so there is nothing to prescribe.

In the EU, a substance or mixture intended to be injected is not considered a cosmetic product (Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009, Article 2(2)); the EU borderline manual adds that a product in a vial or ampoule for use by injection cannot be considered a cosmetic product, and should not be marketed with a device that could allow injection or delivery below the epidermis. Whether a product qualifies as a cosmetic is decided case by case by national competent authorities, and the manual says an anti-wrinkle product that significantly restores, corrects or modifies physiological functions by exerting a pharmacological, immunological or metabolic action does not qualify as one (version 5.5, June 2025).

In Portugal, INFARMED states that products administered by injection are not considered cosmetics (as of 25 September 2026), and medicines intended for parenteral administration are subject to medical prescription by law (Estatuto do Medicamento, Art 114(1)(d)).

In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that injectable cosmetics do not exist; an injectable product offered as a cosmetic is irregular. Products with 'GHK' in the product name appear as notified cosmetics in ANVISA's public cosmetics data (221 entries, 25 September 2026), and ANVISA cancelled several GHK-Cu cosmetic processes on 29 April 2026 without published reasons (RE 1.771/2026).

In the UAE, the medicines law (Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024) defines cosmetics as products with a medical effect on the skin, hair or nails, and whether a product requires an Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) marketing authorisation, and in which category, is determined by an EDE classification letter based on its presentation, composition, use and design. In Dubai, peptide products may be prescribed, dispensed or administered only by licensed, authorised professionals in a licensed health facility (DHA, 29 July 2026); in Abu Dhabi, physicians may prescribe peptide therapies only for clinical indications supported by available scientific evidence, after a documented eligibility assessment and with informed consent that covers benefits, uncertainties, risks, alternatives and the product's regulatory approval status (DoH, 31 July 2026).

Explanation: That is a mechanism argument. There are no randomized trials of injected GHK-Cu, so 'works better' has no evidence behind it.
Correct answer: The topical form has small-trial support; injection rests on anecdote, commonly irritates, and in the US sits outside the Category 1 listing.

SNAP-25 mimics (Argireline and its longer cousin SNAP-8) and Leuphasyl, an enkephalin analogue, are meant to quieten expression lines. Oral collagen peptides are swallowed, not applied. All three families have a trial record, and in all three the question that matters most is who funded it.

units.text: In the UK, a peptide serum is a cosmetic: its responsible person needs a safety assessment and must notify the regulator before sale, and must be able to prove its claims. Oral collagen is a food supplement: no food may claim to prevent, treat or cure disease, and only authorised health claims may be used. In May 2026 the UK advertising regulator ruled a peptide serum's 'clinically proven' lifting claim misleading because the study behind it was small and uncontrolled.

In the EU, a peptide serum sold as a cosmetic needs a responsible person in the EU, a safety assessment with a product safety report and electronic notification to the Commission before it is placed on the market (Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009), and its claims must be supported by adequate and verifiable evidence (Regulation (EU) No 655/2013). Food labelling and advertising may not claim that a food prevents, treats or cures a disease, and health claims on foods are prohibited unless authorised: the Commission refused a claim that a collagen peptide mixture maintains skin health by increasing elasticity and reducing wrinkles, because cause and effect was not established (Regulation (EU) No 1154/2014), and the EU Register lists no authorised claim for collagen itself (searched 25 September 2026).

In Portugal, INFARMED is the competent authority for cosmetics (Decreto-Lei 23/2025), and borderline products must be assessed case by case by the Responsible Person, taking all their characteristics into account (INFARMED, as of 25 September 2026). For food supplement notification, there is no evaluation of the product or validation of labelling; control is carried out afterwards by sampling and may take place at any time (DGAV, as of 25 September 2026).

In Brazil, cosmetic labelling must not contain trade names, brands, images, electronic links or wording that represent therapeutic claims attributed to the use of the product or its ingredients (RDC 907/2024, art. 12). Under ANVISA's January 2025 food supplement guidance, an approved claim is that bioactive hydrolysed collagen peptides with an average molecular weight of 2 kDa help maintain skin health.

In the UAE, the medicines law (Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024) treats food supplements, oral products that support the diet and do not treat, diagnose or prevent disease, as medical products regulated by the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE): oral collagen products are registered with the EDE as general-sale-list health products rather than medicines, while ordinary cosmetics need a conformity certificate from the Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology under Cabinet Resolution 18/2014. Advertising any medical product, social media included, requires EDE approval. In Dubai, the DHA's rules for health facilities ban misleading or unproven peptide claims, such as anti-ageing, cell regeneration or improved appearance, unless the use is within the product's approved status (29 July 2026); in Abu Dhabi, the DoH bars healthcare providers from promoting peptide therapies with misleading or …

Worked example
Two trials, one peptide: LL-37.
LL-37, the skin's own cathelicidin, is the one repair peptide with two randomized trials in hard-to-heal venous leg ulcers. Read them in order.
First trial (2014)
Positive at low dose
First-in-human, randomized, dose-ranging; 34 patients
Second trial (2021)
Negative in the full cohort
Multicentre phase IIb, placebo-controlled; only a post hoc subgroup signal
Who ran them
The developer, both times
Sponsorship does not make a trial wrong; it is one more reason to wait for replication
Grade
C — inconsistent
A small positive trial followed by an adequately powered negative one
Callout: A small positive trial is a hypothesis. LL-37 is what happens when someone tests it.

If you practise in the UK, the route for unlicensed medicines works differently, and lesson 7.2 sets it out.

In the EU, a medicine prepared in a pharmacy on prescription for an individual patient (magistral formula), or to a pharmacopoeia for the pharmacy's own patients (officinal formula), falls outside Directive 2001/83/EC and needs no marketing authorisation under it (Article 3), and each member state may, under its own law, allow an unauthorised medicine for an individual patient on a professional's bona fide unsolicited order, under that professional's direct personal responsibility (Article 5(1)). No centrally authorised medicine containing GHK-Cu, BPC-157 or TB-500 was found in the Union Register or in EMA's data on authorised, refused and withdrawn medicines (searched 25 September 2026).

In Portugal, a magistral formula is a medicine prepared in a community or hospital pharmacy, under a pharmacist's responsibility, on a medical prescription that names the patient, and the prescribing physician must satisfy themselves of its safety and efficacy (Decreto-Lei 95/2004). Compounded medicines may use only raw materials listed in the Portuguese pharmacopoeia, the European pharmacopoeia or another European pharmacopoeia, or in compendial scientific documentation, and one containing any other raw material may not be prescribed.

In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that any substance must have passed efficacy and safety assessment before it can be compounded, and that compounding may only be individual, on presentation of a medical prescription, by a compounding pharmacy licensed by local health surveillance. The same notice says BPC-157 and TB-500 are not authorised as food supplements, and that products presented as peptides called GHK-CU, BPC-157, and TB-500 promising aesthetic effects or health improvements are not registered with ANVISA.

In the UAE, the medicines law (Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024, in force 2 January 2025) exempts medical products compounded in licensed compounding pharmacies from the requirement for a marketing approval from the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE). In Dubai, the DHA's rules for health facilities prohibit circulating, prescribing, dispensing, administering or using any peptide product unless it is registered or licensed with the EDE (29 July 2026); in Abu Dhabi, the DoH treats peptides as emerging, non-monographed, high-risk substances, and novel substances of unknown risk may be compounded only if monographed, a component of an approved medicine or listed on the DoH's register of compounded substances (compounding standard, August 2026).

units.text:
Mechanism
A follicle that runs its own hormones.
Human scalp hair follicles kept alive in the laboratory answer corticotropin-releasing hormone by making ACTH and α-MSH and secreting cortisol, with a feedback loop like the adrenal axis. They also run a growth hormone and IGF-1 loop of their own. Locally made dihydrotestosterone shrinks genetically susceptible scalp follicles, the process behind pattern hair loss. Growing follicles are shielded from immune attack, and alopecia areata begins when that shield fails.
Local stress axis: CRH → ACTH → cortisol, with feedback
Local androgen switch: testosterone → DHT in the scalp
Immune privilege: its collapse drives alopecia areata
Narration: Each hair follicle behaves like a small gland. When researchers keep human scalp follicles alive in culture, the follicles answer corticotropin-releasing hormone the way the pituitary and adrenal glands do…

Human evidence
Two trials, 1,200 adults, one approval.
When immune privilege fails, the attack depends on cytokine signals that JAK inhibitors interrupt. Two randomized phase 3 trials tested oral baricitinib in 1,200 adults with severe alopecia areata. In the US, FDA approved baricitinib for adults with severe alopecia areata on 13 June 2022. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades it A.
adults with severe alopecia areata in the two phase 3 trials of baricitinib (2022)
At 36 weeks, up to 39% of patients on baricitinib had at least 80% of their scalp hair, against 3–6% on placebo
What it means: Interrupting the immune signalling behind collapsed privilege regrows hair in severe alopecia areata. That is approval-grade evidence (A), and it shows what real follicle evidence looks like.
What it does not mean: It says nothing about pattern hair loss, cosmetic thinning or any pe…

units.text: In the UK, baricitinib is licensed for severe alopecia areata in adults, and NICE did not recommend it for NHS use in October 2023, on cost-effectiveness.

In the EU, baricitinib (Olumiant) has been centrally authorised since 13 February 2017; its indications include severe alopecia areata in adults and adolescents aged 12 and over, and it is prescription-only, started by a doctor experienced in the condition (EMA). Since EMA's January 2023 review, JAK inhibitors including Olumiant should be used in people aged 65 or over, at raised cardiovascular or cancer risk, or long-term smokers only if no suitable alternative exists, and this applies to alopecia areata.
In Portugal, Olumiant (baricitinib) is classified as a restricted-prescription medicine (MSRM restrita - Alínea a), according to INFARMED's Infomed register on 25 September 2026.

In Brazil, baricitinib (Olumiant) has been registered by ANVISA since 26 November 2018, and its current label includes severe alopecia areata in adults and adolescents aged 12 or over weighing at least 30 kg (checked 25 September 2026).

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023, and the medicines law is Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024. The EDE register lists Olumiant (baricitinib) tablets, registered since 8 June 2017, as Prescription Only and files them under rheumatic diseases; it does not show whether alopecia areata is an approved UAE indication (25 September 2026).

Lesson 5.2 · Concept
Five receptors, one family of hormones.
Skin makes proopiomelanocortin (POMC) and cuts it into ACTH, α-MSH and β-endorphin, and the same cells carry the receptors that answer them. Those peptides act on five melanocortin receptors. MC1R drives pigment in skin and hair, MC2R answers ACTH in the adrenal gland, MC3R and MC4R act in the brain on appetite, and MC5R governs sebum. Which receptors a drug reaches decides what else it does.
MC1R: pigment of skin and hair
MC2R: adrenal · MC5R: sebum
MC3R and MC4R: appetite, in the brain

Human evidence

Two phase 3 trials in erythropoietic protoporphyria, against a three-volunteer pilot and a ten-man erectile-dysfunction study from the 1990s. The Peptide Pocket Guide rates Melanotan II C and the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide D; with no trial of tanning, this course uses D.

units.text: In the UK, afamelanotide is licensed under exceptional circumstances and prescribed only in specialist porphyria centres, and NICE did not recommend it for NHS use (July 2023).

In the EU, afamelanotide (Scenesse implant) is authorised for erythropoietic protoporphyria, under exceptional circumstances (European Commission, 22 December 2014), and is prescribed only by specialists in recognised EPP centres.

In Portugal, Scenesse is authorised through the EU procedure but classified as a restricted-prescription medicine for exclusive hospital use (MSRM restrita, alínea a), and no presentation is marketed in Portugal (INFARMED's Infomed register, 25 September 2026).

In Brazil, no registered medicine containing afamelanotide (Scenesse) was found: ANVISA's open-data register and its online medicines search returned no match on 25 September 2026, and the substance is absent from ANVISA's substance dictionary.

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023, and the medicines law is Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024. An ingredient and product-name search of the EDE register found no registered product containing afamelanotide, and none named Scenesse (25 September 2026).

The evidence
Sixty-nine hours against forty-one.
Erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) is a rare disorder in which sunlight causes acute, severe pain. In the US phase 3 trial, adults on afamelanotide spent a median 69.4 hours in direct sunlight without pain over six months, against 40.8 hours on placebo. The European trial also showed more pain-free time and fewer phototoxic reactions. Both trials were funded by the manufacturer.

units.text:
Safety signals
What the case reports show.
The harms of Melanotan II come from case reports and reviews, so they show what can happen without telling you how often. Reported skin effects include darkening and growth of existing moles, crops of new and sometimes atypical naevi, and dark bands in the nails. At least five melanomas have been reported during or after use, each in someone with other risk factors, so causation is unproven. Systemic reports include ischaemic priapism needing surgery and a stimulant-like toxic reaction with rhabdomyolysis, and FDA lists posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome among published serious events.

Melanoma: reported, causation unproven
Systemic: priapism, rhabdomyolysis, encephalopathy

Lesson 5.3 · Concept
A Wnt switch and a zinc question.
PTD-DBM joins a cell-penetrating peptide to a short decoy sequence that stops the protein CXXC5 from binding Dishevelled. Freed from that brake, Wnt/β-catenin signalling rises, and in mice hair regrew faster. Its developers also found CXXC5 raised in human balding scalp. units.text:
Lesson 6.1 · Mechanism
Two hormones, two layers of skin.
Growth hormone acts mostly in the dermis. Its receptor is expressed more by fibroblasts than by keratinocytes, and it increases fibroblast numbers and supports collagen synthesis. IGF-1, made locally by fibroblasts and melanocytes, reaches keratinocytes through the IGF-1 receptor and makes them divide. Human hair follicles even run their own small growth-hormone loop in the laboratory. With age, GH secretion and IGF-1 fall steadily; this is the somatopause.
GH: dermal fibroblasts and collagen
IGF-1: keratinocyte proliferation, supplied locally
Somatopause: GH and IGF-1 fall with age

What changes in practice
Deficiency is a diagnosis. Decline is ageing.
In healthy older adults, randomized trials of growth hormone show small shifts in body composition, about 2 kg less fat and 2 kg more lean mass, with more oedema, joint pain, carpal tunnel syndrome and a trend towards diabetes. Strength and endurance change little. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades its advice against treatment A; graded on the trials themselves the evidence is B, and the conclusion is the same. In the US, as of September 2026, knowingly distributing growth hormone for anti-ageing is a federal offence.

units.text: In the UK, somatropin is a prescription-only medicine licensed for growth hormone deficiency and specific growth disorders, and a Class C controlled drug.

In the EU, somatropin medicines have been authorised since the 1980s, through central and national procedures, for growth hormone replacement and for short stature in specific childhood conditions (EMA, 2012). The centrally authorised Omnitrope (since 12 April 2006) is prescription-only, and treatment is started and monitored by a doctor experienced in growth disorders.

In Portugal, somatropin medicines are authorised as restricted-prescription medicines, reserved for conditions diagnosed only in hospital or specialised settings, and INFARMED's register gives them no narcotic classification (25 September 2026). Growth hormone is distributed free of charge through hospitals with endocrinology or paediatric services, and a national commission (CNNHC) sets the conditions for its administration.

In Brazil, somatropin is registered for replacement therapy in adults with marked growth hormone deficiency, and it is a controlled substance on List C5 (anabolic substances) that needs a special-control prescription in two copies (RDC 1.036/2026). The Federal Council of Medicine's Resolution 1.999/2012, in force in September 2026, bars the use of hormones, including growth hormone, except in diagnosed deficiencies where replacement shows evidence of scientifically proven benefit.

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023; the medicines law is Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024, which prohibits advertising semi-controlled products to the public. Somatropin is registered with the EDE and is on the federal list of semi-controlled medical products (MOHAP Ministerial Decision 306/2023), and every somatropin entry in the EDE register is dispensed as a semi-controlled drug (25 September 2026).

Lesson 6.2 · Concept
One axis, four ways in.
Somatropin is growth hormone itself. GHRH analogues (sermorelin, tesamorelin, CJC-1295) stimulate the pituitary's GHRH receptor. Ghrelin-receptor agonists (ipamorelin, GHRP-2, GHRP-6 and the oral ibutamoren, MK-677) stimulate GH release through a second pituitary receptor. IGF-1 analogues such as IGF-1 LR3 bypass the pituitary altogether. They are sold as one family, and the next moments take them apart.
Replace: somatropin
Stimulate: GHRH analogues and ghrelin-receptor agonists
Bypass: IGF-1 analogues

units.text: In the EU, somatropin has been authorised since the 1980s for growth hormone replacement and short stature in specific childhood conditions, while tesamorelin has no marketing authorisation (its application was withdrawn on 21 June 2012). No centrally authorised medicine containing sermorelin, ipamorelin or CJC-1295 was found in the Union Register or EMA's data (25 September 2026), and ibutamoren (MK-677) is not an authorised medicine: its orphan designation for growth hormone deficiency (20 June 2017) is, as EMA states, not a marketing authorisation.

In Portugal, no medicine containing tesamorelin, sermorelin, ipamorelin, CJC-1295 or ibutamoren (MK-677) is listed in INFARMED's Infomed register, which includes authorised, lapsed and revoked products (25 September 2026). Compounded medicines may use only raw materials listed in the Portuguese or European pharmacopoeia, another European pharmacopoeia or compendial scientific documentation, and one containing any other raw material may not be prescribed (Decreto-Lei 95/2004).

In Brazil, no registered medicine containing tesamorelin or sermorelin was found in ANVISA's register (25 September 2026), and ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that CJC-1295 and ipamorelin products are not registered with ANVISA and that any substance must have passed efficacy and safety assessment before it can be compounded. Ibutamoren is not a registered medicine, and ANVISA refused the clinical-trial petitions for ibutamoren mesylate on 9 June 2026.

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023; the medicines law is Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024. Somatropin is registered and dispensed as a semi-controlled drug, while no registered product containing tesamorelin, sermorelin, ipamorelin, CJC-1295 or ibutamoren was found in the EDE register (25 September 2026). In Dubai, the DHA prohibits prescribing, dispensing or using any peptide product that is not registered or licensed with the EDE (29 July 2026); in Abu Dhabi, the DoH's compounding standard treats peptides as non-monographed, high-risk substances and lets novel substances of unknown risk be compounded only if monographed, part of an approved medicine or listed on the DoH Registry for Compounded Substances (August 2026).

Name the indication before the molecule.
When a patient asks about a growth-hormone peptide, three answers come first. Which molecule, exactly, including whether 'CJC' means with or without DAC. What stands behind it, whether approval-grade trials for one indication, hormone levels only, or nothing. And where it stands in the US today, read off the live FDA lists. Tesamorelin's GRADE A belongs to HIV-associated abdominal fat and transfers to nothing else.

units.text: In the UK, MHRA's products database holds no product information for tesamorelin, sermorelin or ipamorelin (searched 25 September 2026), so any of them would reach a patient only as an unlicensed medicine. An unlicensed special needs a clinical need that no licensed medicine meets.

In the EU, tesamorelin has no marketing authorisation (its application was withdrawn on 21 June 2012), and no centrally authorised medicine containing sermorelin or ipamorelin was found in the Union Register or EMA's data (25 September 2026). EU law lets each member state, under its own legislation, allow an unauthorised medicine for an individual patient on a bona fide unsolicited order from an authorised health professional, under that professional's direct personal responsibility (Directive 2001/83/EC, Article 5(1)).

In Portugal, no medicine containing tesamorelin, sermorelin or ipamorelin is listed in INFARMED's Infomed register, which includes authorised, lapsed and revoked products (25 September 2026). INFARMED may authorise exceptional use (AUE) of a medicine without a marketing authorisation, for example when it is clinically justified as indispensable and no authorised alternative exists (Estatuto do Medicamento).

In Brazil, no registered medicine containing tesamorelin or sermorelin was found in ANVISA's register (25 September 2026). ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that products presented as peptides called ipamorelin that promise aesthetic effects or health improvements are not registered with ANVISA, and that some injectable peptides are not regularised in any category and are therefore illegal for any health use, including aesthetic use.

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023; the medicines law is Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024. No registered product containing tesamorelin, sermorelin or ipamorelin was found in the EDE register (25 September 2026). In Dubai, the DHA prohibits prescribing, dispensing or using any peptide product that is not registered or licensed with the EDE and bans misleading or unproven anti-ageing claims for peptides (29 July 2026); in Abu Dhabi, physicians may prescribe peptide therapies only for clinical indications supported by available scientific evidence, after a documented eligibility assessment and with informed consent that covers the product's regulatory approval status (DoH, 31 July 2026).

Lesson 6.3 · Recognition
What too much growth hormone looks like.
Sustained GH excess changes skin in ways you can see. In acromegaly, glycosaminoglycan deposits and oedema make the face, hands and feet puffy and thick; the skin turns oily with large pores; sweating increases; skin tags and acanthosis nigricans appear. units.text:
Four registers
Does raising IGF-1 cause cancer?
The honest answer has four parts, and each has its own source. Keep them apart, or a mechanism will be heard as a measured risk.
Mechanism
Plausible
IGF-1 receptor signalling drives cell proliferation and survival, which gives any IGF-1-raising product a theoretical concern
Human observation
Modest associations
In large studies, higher natural IGF-1 goes with slightly higher risks of prostate, breast, colorectal and thyroid cancer; reverse causation is not excluded. In one Ecuadorian cohort, people with GH-receptor deficiency had almost no cancer.
Acromegaly
Slightly raised, inconsistently
Pooled studies show about 1.5 times the expected cancer incidence, with the highest estimates from small single-centre series; a Danish nationwide cohort found no clear rise
GH replacement
Largely reassuring
No clear raised risk in 23,984 GH-treated child…

units.text:
Lesson 7.1 · Concept
GRADE rates certainty in an effect, one outcome at a time.
GRADE sorts the evidence on a specific question into four levels of certainty: high, moderate, low and very low. The rating applies to a body of evidence for one outcome, never to a single study or to a molecule. Randomized trials start high and observational studies start low; certainty then falls for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision or suspected publication bias, and occasionally rises for a very large effect. Both Hormonaly guides print the letters A to D for the same idea, adapted, and attach each letter to a specific use.
Four levels, applied to a body of evidence
Five named reasons to rate down
The letter belongs to a use, never to a molecule

Lesson 7.2 · Concept
Two compounding routes, one strict order.
In the US, section 503A lets a licensed pharmacist or physician compound for an identified patient on a prescription, exempt from new-drug approval, adequate directions for use and good manufacturing practice. The bulk substance must meet a USP or NF monograph; failing that, be a component of an approved drug; failing that, appear on FDA's 503A bulks list. It must also come from an FDA-registered establishment with a valid certificate of analysis. Section 503B outsourcing facilities register with FDA, work to good manufacturing practice under inspection, and may compound without patient-specific prescriptions.

units.text: In the EU, medicines prepared in a pharmacy on prescription for an individual patient (magistral formulas) or to a pharmacopoeia for the pharmacy's own patients (officinal formulas) are outside Directive 2001/83/EC (Article 3). Pharmacists who prepare medicines solely for retail supply in dispensing pharmacies are also exempt from manufacturing authorisation (Article 40(2)).

In Portugal, a magistral formula is prepared in a community or hospital pharmacy on a medical prescription naming the patient, under a pharmacist's responsibility (Decreto-Lei 95/2004). Compounded medicines may use only raw materials listed in the Portuguese or European pharmacopoeia, another European pharmacopoeia or compendial scientific documentation, and one containing any other raw material may not be prescribed.

In Brazil, a magistral preparation is made individually by a pharmacy against a prescription from an authorised professional (RDC 96/2008). ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that any substance must have passed efficacy and safety assessment before it can be compounded, and that compounding may take place only individually, on a medical prescription, in a pharmacy licensed by local health surveillance.

In the UAE, where the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has regulated medical products since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023, products compounded in licensed compounding pharmacies are exempt from marketing approval under Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024 (Art. 5(2)), although such a pharmacy may not copy an EDE-approved product unless no commercial product can deliver the expected benefit, nor formulate products for research, development or experimentation (Art. 95). In Abu Dhabi, the DoH's compounding standard (August 2026) treats peptides as high-risk substances and lets novel substances of unknown risk be compounded only if monographed, a component of an approved medicine or listed on the DoH Registry for Compounded Substances. In Dubai, the DHA prohibits prescribing, dispensing or using any peptide product that is not registered or licensed with the EDE (29 July 2026).

Concept
What a certificate can and cannot prove.
A certificate of analysis is the supplier's own report on a named lot. Mass spectrometry checks identity, and a careful certificate prints the expected mass beside the observed one. HPLC gives purity as a percentage, which says nothing about what the impurities are. Endotoxin, microbial, water, counter-ion, metal and solvent results complete it. A certificate cannot prove that the vial in your hand came from that lot, how it was stored since, or that it is sterile and suitable to inject.
Identity: mass spectrometry, observed against expected
Purity: an HPLC percentage, impurities unnamed
Suitability to inject needs sterility, endotoxin and the right lot

units.text: In the EU, a product is a medicine by presentation (presented as treating or preventing disease) or by function (restoring, correcting or modifying physiological functions by a pharmacological, immunological or metabolic action), and where it could be both a medicine and another regulated product, medicines law applies (Directive 2001/83/EC, Articles 1(2) and 2(2)). The Directive's research exclusion covers medicinal products intended for research and development trials (Article 3(3)).

In Portugal, a medicine is any substance or combination of substances presented as having properties for treating or preventing disease in human beings or its symptoms, or which may be used in or administered to human beings to make a medical diagnosis or to restore, correct or modify physiological functions by exerting a pharmacological, immunological or metabolic action (Estatuto do Medicamento). Making, selling, supplying or administering medicines without the required authorisations or registrations is an administrative offence punishable by a fine from €2,000 up to 15% of turnover or €180,000, whichever is lower.

In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that some injectable peptides are not regularised in any category (food, medicine, cosmetic or food supplement) and so are illegal for any health use, including aesthetic use. ANVISA also stated in July 2026 that an investigational medicine is used only in authorised clinical research.

In the UAE, Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024 has, since 2 January 2025, barred importing, distributing, possessing, selling, displaying or using any medical product without a marketing approval from the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE), the federal regulator of medical products since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023. In Dubai, the DHA prohibits using any peptide product intended for research use on humans, or for therapeutic purposes outside an approved study or clinical trial, and bars facilities from buying peptide products from websites, social media or unverifiable suppliers (29 July 2026). In Abu Dhabi, the DoH's compounding standard (August 2026) prohibits compounding from unapproved or unknown-source substances, or from substances not on the DoH Registry for Compounded Substances, unless the DoH permits it.

Regulatory status (outside the US)
Selling and advertising peptides outside the US.
Outside the US, whether a peptide is regulated as a medicine turns on what is claimed for it and on what it is and does, not on the category a seller chooses, and a medicine without a marketing authorisation may not be sold, supplied or advertised. Advertising a prescription-only medicine to the public is prohibited, or needs the regulator's prior approval.

units.text: In the UK, MHRA decides whether a product is a medicine from its claims, including websites and social media, and from its form and the way it is used. A medicine with no UK marketing authorisation may not be sold, supplied or advertised. MHRA classes injectable melanotan products as medicines, and its largest seizure of unlicensed weight-loss medicines, in May 2026, included peptide products. Prescription-only medicines may not be advertised to the public at all: a clinic may promote 'treatment for lines and wrinkles' without naming the medicine, and in February 2026 the UK advertising regulator ruled that influencer posts tagging a weight-loss injection were adverts for a prescription-only medicine. GMC guidance requires doctors to examine a patient physically before prescribing an injectable cosmetic medicine.

In the EU, member states must prohibit any advertising of a medicine that has no marketing authorisation, and any advertising of prescription-only medicines to the general public, where advertising includes any inducement designed to promote prescription, supply, sale or consumption (Directive 2001/83/EC, Articles 86 to 88). EU audiovisual law also bans audiovisual commercial communications for prescription-only medicines and medical treatment, and video-sharing platforms must apply this to advertising on their services, including advertising they do not sell themselves (Directive 2010/13/EU).

In Portugal, advertising a medicine without a valid national authorisation or registration, or one authorised under Articles 92 and 93, is prohibited, prescription-only medicines may be advertised only in technical media for health professionals, and the advertiser, the agency, anyone disseminating the advertising and the owner of the medium are all liable (Estatuto do Medicamento). Health advertising practices fall under Decreto-Lei 238/2015, which bans false claims of guaranteed cure or results or of absence of side effects and is enforced by the Health Regulatory Authority (ERS).

Lesson 7.3 · Concept
Off-label needs a label.
Off-label prescribing means using an approved drug for a use its labelling does not cover, and FDA accepts it as clinical judgment. A never-approved peptide has no label to depart from, so prescribing it is use of an unapproved drug. Introducing an unapproved new drug into interstate commerce is a prohibited act under the FD&C Act, and FDA's 2020 warning letter to a compounding pharmacy named BPC-157 and GHK-Cu on exactly this basis.

Compounded is still unapproved

units.text: The UK sorts products the same way, by claim, form and use, into cosmetics, food and medicines; lesson 7.2 set out its route for unlicensed medicines.

In the EU, a product is a medicine by presentation or by pharmacological, immunological or metabolic function, and where it could also fall under another product law, medicines law applies (Directive 2001/83/EC, Articles 1(2) and 2(2)); anything intended to be ingested, inhaled, injected or implanted is not a cosmetic (Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009, Article 2(2)). Food supplements are foods, and a health claim on a food is prohibited unless it is authorised and on the EU lists of authorised claims (Directive 2002/46/EC; Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006, Article 10(1)).

In Portugal, INFARMED is the competent authority for cosmetics and states that products administered by ingestion, inhalation, injection or implantation into the body are not cosmetics (read 25 September 2026). Food supplements are meant to maintain the body's homeostasis, not to prevent, treat or cure disease, and must be notified to DGAV before sale; DGAV warns that notification does not mean a supplement is authorised or compliant.

In Brazil, cosmetic labelling may not carry therapeutic claims for the product or its ingredients (RDC 907/2024, art. 12), and ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that injectable cosmetics do not exist and that, if a product is offered in this form, it is an irregular cosmetic. A food supplement is by definition a product for oral ingestion by healthy people (RDC 243/2018), and it may use only constituents on ANVISA's authorised list (IN 28/2018).

In the UAE, Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024 makes cosmetics with a medical effect on the skin, hair or nails, and food supplements, medical products regulated by the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE, the federal regulator of medical products since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023), while ordinary cosmetics need a MoIAT conformity certificate (Cabinet Resolution 18/2014); an EDE classification letter settles whether a product needs EDE marketing authorisation and in which regulatory category. In Abu Dhabi, the DoH keeps topical cosmetic peptides with no systemic effect on existing pathways as low-risk products, while systemic, regenerative or weakly evidenced peptides face enhanced controls (31 July 2026).

Explanation: A claim to affect structure or function, such as 'regenerates cells', makes it a drug.

Explanation: Accurate as stated: topical GHK-Cu's only indexed trial measured healing after laser resurfacing. It is a real trial, of a different outcome.

Fictional case
'Just prescribe it off-label.'
A 52-year-old patient, three weeks after a fractional laser treatment, asks you to prescribe compounded BPC-157 injections 'off-label' to speed healing. She has found a pharmacy willing to make it and shows you its certificate of analysis. This is a fictional case built from the module's sources, and one response is clearly best.
BPC-157 has no approval, so there is no label to go off
It has no 503A route; FDA staff advised against listing it
A certificate describes a lot and creates no route
Role version (prescriber): You decline, explain, and document the request, the product's status in those words, the evidence you quoted and the alternatives you offered.
Role version (clinical-staff): If a patient asks you to arrange or give a compounded or research peptide, record the request and the product details and pass it to the prescriber; do not…

units.text:
What do you do?
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Prescribe it as off-label use and file the certificate in her chart.
Explanation: Off-label presupposes an approved drug. BPC-157 has no approval and no 503A route, FDA has warned a compounder about it, and a certificate changes neither fact.
Correct answer: Decline to prescribe it. Explain the evidence and the US status in plain terms, return to the aftercare plan her treating clinician set, and record her request, what you explained and her decision.
Explanation: Right. You keep the conversation, give her the real category and the grade, and leave a chart note a reviewer can follow.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Suggest she buy research-grade BPC-157 with a good certificate and come back for monitoring.
Explanation: Research-use-only products are labelled not for use in humans, and the Peptide Pocket Guide tr…
In the EU, no centrally authorised medicine containing BPC-157 was found in the Union Register or in EMA's data on authorised, refused and withdrawn medicines (searched 25 September 2026).

In Portugal, no medicine containing BPC-157 is listed in INFARMED's Infomed register, which includes authorised, lapsed and revoked products (searched 25 September 2026). A compounded medicine may use only raw materials listed in the Portuguese or European pharmacopoeia, another European pharmacopoeia or compendial scientific documentation (Decreto-Lei 95/2004).

In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that BPC-157 is not authorised for use as a food supplement, and that any substance must have passed efficacy and safety assessment before it can be compounded.

In the UAE, no registered product containing BPC-157 was found in the register of the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE), the federal regulator of medical products since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023 (searched 25 September 2026). In Dubai, the DHA prohibits any peptide product that is not registered or licensed with the EDE (29 July 2026). In Abu Dhabi, the DoH's compounding standard (August 2026) treats peptides as high-risk substances and lets novel substances of unknown risk be compounded only if monographed, a component of an approved medicine or listed on the DoH Registry for Compounded Substances.

units.text: In the EU, a member state may, under its own legislation, allow an unauthorised medicine for an individual patient on a bona fide unsolicited order from an authorised health professional, under that professional's direct personal responsibility (Directive 2001/83/EC, Article 5(1)).

In Portugal, a physician who prescribes a magistral formula must satisfy themselves of its safety and efficacy, including possible interactions (Decreto-Lei 95/2004), and a patient-specific exceptional-use authorisation (AUE) always needs an individual clinical justification that the medicine is indispensable (Deliberação 840/2023, 31 August 2023).

In Brazil, ANVISA stated in September 2025 that using an unregistered imported medicine is entirely the responsibility of the patient and the prescribing physician, and in April 2025 that off-label prescribing of a registered medicine rests on the physician's judgment that, for a given patient, benefits outweigh risks.

In the UAE, Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024 allows prescribing outside a product's leaflet, or a product never submitted to the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE, the federal regulator of medical products since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023) for marketing approval, only when necessary, with no equivalent alternative available and with the patient's approval (Art. 42(1)). In Abu Dhabi, the DoH requires a documented eligibility assessment before peptide therapy and documented informed consent covering expected benefits, uncertainties, risks, alternatives and the product's regulatory approval status (31 July 2026). In Dubai, the DHA does not permit injections or intravenous therapies for 'wellness', 'recovery', 'detoxification' or 'energy enhancement' without a documented medical indication and treatment plan (29 July 2026).

From the vial to the note
Decide what you tell her, what FDA's record shows and what you write down.
What do you tell her?
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Agree to supervise once she signs a consent form.
Explanation: Research use only is not a clinical pathway. Do not prescribe, supply, supervise or recommend a research-use-only product.
Correct answer: Decline to supervise, supply or recommend it: a research-use-only product stays outside clinical care.
Explanation: Right. FDA reads intended use from claims, marketing and the circumstances of sale, so the 'not for use in humans' disclaimer changes nothing about a vial sold with injection instructions.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Agree to supervise if the certificate shows high purity.
Explanation: A certificate of analysis, however clean, cannot convert that vial into a pharmaceutical: sterility, manufac…

GHK-Cu appears in three products: a cream sold 'for the look of fine lines', the same cream sold 'to regenerate skin cells', and an injectable vial labelled research use only. In the US, which statement is right?
Explanation: Name the claim and the route, then the regime.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): All three are cosmetics, because the molecule is the same.
Explanation: The regime follows the claim and the route. A structure-or-function claim makes the second cream a drug, and the vial is no cosmetic at all.
Correct answer: The first is a cosmetic; the second makes a drug claim, so it is an unapproved drug; the vial is outside any clinical route.
Explanation: Correct. Claim and route decide the rulebook, whatever the molecule.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): All three are lawful, because GHK-Cu is in Category 1.
Explanation: Category 1 covers 503A compound…

Closing Module 7: which statement keeps evidence, regulatory status and product quality apart?
Explanation: Grade, status and quality: three checks, never one sentence.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): The certificate shows 99% purity, so the peptide is evidence-based and fine to compound.
Explanation: That blends product quality into evidence and legality. Purity says nothing about whether it works or whether any route is lawful.
Correct answer: Topical GHK-Cu: small-trial evidence (C); in the US, non-injectable use sits in 503A Category 1, under evaluation; its certificate can show identity and purity, never sterility or legality.
Explanation: Correct. Three separate answers, each with its own source.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): GHK-Cu is in Category 1, so it is approved for skin and the evidence question is settled.
Explanation: Category 1 is an enforcem…

A single-cell RNA atlas predicts that a skin cell type can make a hormone. What would move that finding toward proof of secretion?
Explanation: Transcriptomic maps predict capacity; secretion and function need protein-level and functional evidence, and clinical use needs human trials.
Correct answer: Showing the hormone protein and its release by those cells, then its effect in tissue or in people.
Explanation: Correct. RNA is the first rung; protein, release and function are the next.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Finding the same RNA in a second atlas.
Explanation: Replicating the RNA confirms the transcript, which is still a prediction about secretion.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Finding the hormone's receptor RNA in neighbouring cells.
Explanation: That predicts a possible receiver; it does not show the hormone is made or released.

Which finding is a local cutaneous feedback loop rather than systemic endocrine signalling?
Explanation: A local loop is made and used within the skin; systemic signals travel through the blood, in either direction.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Skin-made vitamin D3 carried by the blood to the liver.
Explanation: That is the skin supplying a whole-body hormone system: skin to body.
Correct answer: Human scalp follicles in culture secrete cortisol and then reduce their own CRH.
Explanation: Correct. Made, sensed and fed back within the follicle, with no systemic connection.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Thin skin and striae in Cushing syndrome.
Explanation: Circulating cortisol excess acting on the skin: body to skin.

Why can a blood or saliva cortisol level not tell you how much cortisol a patient's skin is generating?
Explanation: Local tissue cortisol and systemic cortisol are separate: the first is a research mechanism, the second is what diagnostic tests measure.
Correct answer: Because 11β-HSD1 regenerates cortisol inside skin cells, and local availability is regulated independently of circulating levels.
Explanation: Correct: a mechanism shown in human skin samples and mice.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Because skin cells cannot make or activate cortisol.
Explanation: They can: skin expresses an HPA-like axis, and 11β-HSD1 regenerates cortisol locally.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Because saliva and blood cortisol tests are unreliable for everything.
Explanation: Late-night salivary cortisol is a first-line test for Cushing's syndrome; it measures systemic cort…

A patient asks whether starting hormone therapy at menopause will stop her wrinkles. Which answer fits the evidence?
Explanation: Separate structural effects (small trials) from visible ageing (large trials) and from indications (symptoms and bone).
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Yes: estrogen rebuilds collagen, so her wrinkles will improve.
Explanation: Small trials show thicker skin, but the largest trials found no difference in wrinkles.
Correct answer: It may thicken the skin a little, the largest trials found no difference in wrinkles, and skin is not a reason to start; hot flashes or vaginal symptoms are worth discussing with a prescriber.
Explanation: Correct: a secondary effect, and an indication-led decision.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): It has no effect on skin at all.
Explanation: Small RCTs do show gains in thickness and collagen; what is unpro…

A colleague says tirzepatide is 'GRADE A', so its effect on the face must be well established. What is wrong with that reasoning?
Explanation: An evidence grade belongs to a statement, not to a molecule. SURMOUNT-1 supports an A for weight loss; facial change rests on a 20-patient imaging study and a patient survey (C to D), and no randomized trial has measured the face.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Nothing: a drug's grade applies to all of its effects.
Explanation: Grades attach to a specific outcome in a specific population. The pivotal trials measured weight and never the face.
Correct answer: Grades attach to outcomes: weight loss is A from large randomized trials, while facial change rests on small observational studies.
Explanation: Correct. One grade per outcome.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Tirzepatide has no GRADE A evidence for anything.
Explan…

Which statement about the gut–skin link is best supported by the evidence?
Explanation: High-fat feeding raises circulating endotoxin in mice and briefly in healthy men; a leading review finds it unproven that restoring barrier function improves disease outside the gut, and Cochrane found little or no patient-rated benefit from probiotics in eczema.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Probiotic capsules reliably clear eczema by repairing the gut barrier.
Explanation: Pooled trials show little or no difference in patient-rated eczema symptoms.
Correct answer: Metabolic endotoxaemia is shown in mice and small human studies, but restoring the gut barrier has not been shown to improve disease outside the gut.
Explanation: Correct. Mechanism in mice and short-term human physiology; no proof that barrier repair helps the skin.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): A zonulin b…

Which statement about topical GHK-Cu keeps its evidence and its regulatory status apart correctly?
Explanation: Mechanism, human evidence and regulatory status are separate registers; GHK-Cu scores differently on each.
Correct answer: It is GRADE C on small trials, and in the US its non-injectable form sits in 503A Category 1, which means under evaluation.
Explanation: Correct. Two separate answers: small-trial human evidence, and an enforcement posture that is not an approval.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Its Category 1 listing shows FDA has found it effective for skin.
Explanation: Category 1 means FDA is still evaluating; it says nothing about efficacy.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Its copper-enzyme mechanism makes its evidence grade A.
Explanation: A plausible mechanism is not human evidence; the trials are small (C).

Oral collagen trials pooled together look positive. What did splitting them by funding and quality show?
Explanation: Funding and study quality can explain a pooled effect; ask who ran the trial before what it showed.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): The benefit held in every subgroup.
Explanation: It did not: independent and high-quality trials showed no effect.
Correct answer: The benefit appeared only in pharmaceutical-funded and lower-quality trials.
Explanation: Correct — Myung and Park, 2025, 23 RCTs.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Independent trials showed harm.
Explanation: No harm signal was reported; the finding is about absence of benefit.

Which statement about afamelanotide and Melanotan II is accurate?
Explanation: Approval attaches to a specific product and indication; a shared receptor transfers neither evidence nor legal standing.
Correct answer: Afamelanotide is approved (EU 2014, US 2019) only for erythropoietic protoporphyria; Melanotan II is approved for no indication, and regulators in the US, UK and Australia have warned about it.
Explanation: Correct. Same receptor family, different molecules, and only one has an approval, for one rare disease.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Afamelanotide's US approval covers cosmetic tanning.
Explanation: The US indication is to increase pain-free light exposure in adults with EPP; tanning is not an approved use.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Melanotan II became approvable once FDA reviewed it for compounding.
Explanation: Its compounding nominat…

A patient asks about a PTD-DBM hair spray. Which grade fits its evidence, and why?
Explanation: Grade the human evidence, then say who produced it; a strong mechanism with no trial in people is D.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): A, because it acts on the central Wnt pathway of hair growth.
Explanation: A plausible pathway is mechanism, and grades rest on human evidence.
Correct answer: D: one 2017 study in mice and scalp tissue from the developer's group, and no human trial published or registered as of September 2026.
Explanation: Correct. Animal and tissue data only, from one group with a commercial link.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): C, because small human trials show regrowth.
Explanation: No human trial of PTD-DBM exists, small or large.

In the US, as of September 2026, which statement about growth-hormone secretagogues and 503A compounding is accurate?
Explanation: Popularity and compounding volume are not regulatory standing; check the live FDA lists and name the date.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Ipamorelin and CJC-1295 are on the 503A bulks list, because clinics compound them widely.
Explanation: Neither is on the list. FDA's advisory committee voted against ipamorelin in 2024, and both 503A nominations were withdrawn.
Correct answer: None of them is on the 503A bulks list; ibutamoren is in FDA's Category 2 for a heart-failure signal, and the ipamorelin and CJC-1295 nominations were withdrawn.
Explanation: Correct, dated to FDA's category documents of April and May 2026.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Sermorelin is an FDA-approved product marketed for adult anti-ageing.
Explanation: No…

Why does a 'low' IGF-1 in a healthy 60-year-old not, on its own, justify growth-hormone therapy?
Explanation: Treat confirmed deficiency, not ageing: age-adjusted ranges plus the healthy-ageing trials.
Correct answer: IGF-1 falls normally with age, and trials in healthy older adults show small body-composition gains with more oedema, joint pain and glucose problems.
Explanation: Correct. The somatopause is physiology, and the trials point against treatment.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Because growth hormone has no effect on skin at all.
Explanation: GH acts on dermal fibroblasts, and GH excess visibly changes skin. The problem is the balance of benefit and harm in healthy adults.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Because IGF-1 cannot be measured reliably.
Explanation: IGF-1 is a standard test. The point is to read it against an age-matched range and to treat…

In GRADE, what does a certainty rating attach to?
Explanation: Name the outcome before you name the grade; risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision and publication bias can each lower it.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): A single well-run trial.
Explanation: GRADE rates a body of evidence, never one study on its own.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): The molecule, across all its uses.
Explanation: The same molecule can be high certainty for one outcome and very low for another.
Correct answer: A body of evidence for a specific outcome.
Explanation: Correct. Certainty belongs to an outcome, across the studies that address it.

Under section 503A, in what order does the statute let a bulk substance qualify for compounding?
Explanation: The statute's routes are hierarchical, and as of September 2026 no peptide sits on the six-substance bulks list.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): The bulks list first, then a monograph, then a component of an approved drug.
Explanation: Reversed. The bulks list is the last route, open only when the first two are not.
Correct answer: A USP or NF monograph first, then a component of an approved drug, then the 503A bulks list, with a valid certificate of analysis in every case.
Explanation: Correct. The routes are hierarchical, and the certificate and a registered manufacturer are conditions throughout.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Any substance whose certificate of analysis shows high purity.
Explanation: A certificate is a condition, never a route on …

The Hormone Cell Atlas (Fei, Huang-Doran et al., Science 2026) read RNA for 379 hormone and receptor genes in about 14 million cells and nuclei from 47 human tissues and predicted which cell types could make or respond to hormones. Its own authors call these predictions putative and hypothesis-generating: RNA shows capacity, not secretion or effect. Treat any 'skin has receptors for it' product claim as a hypothesis until protein, function and a human trial back it. A few skin outputs are established in people, such as vitamin D3 formed under UVB and released into the blood.

Senescent cells accumulate in human epidermis and dermis with age, and in one cohort their number tracked with wrinkles and perceived age: an association. Their secretions (the SASP: IL-6, IL-8, matrix-degrading enzymes) were defined in cultured cells. Evidence that clearing senescent cells improves ageing comes from mice; human data are small open-label or exploratory pilots measuring tissue markers. The one randomized study in skin (topical rapamycin, a senomorphic, 2019) was small and exploratory: it lowered p16, and clinical change was only described. No adequately sized trial with clinical skin-ageing outcomes was found (September 2026). In mice, clearing senescent cells during healing slowed wound closure. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide advises confining senolytics to clinical trials. This course gives no doses or product advice; daily sunscreen and topical retino…

Most 'cortisol face' is puffiness from sleep, alcohol, salt and weight, as the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide describes it. Endogenous Cushing's syndrome is rare (two to three new cases per million people a year), and its commonest form comes from a glucocorticoid the patient is using, so ask about tablets, inhalers, injections and creams, including skin-lighteners. The features that best discriminate Cushing's are easy bruising, facial plethora, proximal muscle weakness and reddish-purple striae wider than 1 cm; a round face alone is a weak signal. If several are present and progressing, the next step is formal testing arranged by a prescriber and an endocrinologist, not a supplement or a consumer cortisol panel. Local skin cortisol (11β-HSD1) is a research mechanism with no approved treatment.

Estrogen acts on receptors in skin. In small trials, hormone therapy thickened skin and raised collagen (graded C here). The largest trial on facial skin (485 women, 48 weeks) and a four-year trial in recently menopausal women found no difference in wrinkles. In the US, as of February 2026, approved uses of menopausal hormone therapy are hot flashes, vaginal and vulvar symptoms and, for some products, preventing bone loss; skin is not an indication and is never the reason to start. Compounded 'bioidentical' hormones lack efficacy and safety data, and an over-the-counter 'hormone cream' is an unapproved drug under US rules. In the UK, HRT products are prescription-only medicines licensed for oestrogen-deficiency symptoms and, for some, for preventing osteoporosis; skin is not among their uses, and a compounded 'bioidentical' hormone is an unlicensed medicine that MHRA guidance places behi…

'Ozempic face' describes facial hollowing and laxity during weight loss on incretin drugs. Mechanism: losing fat deflates the superficial facial fat compartments and unmasks laxity already present. Human evidence is observational and small: one retrospective imaging study of 20 patients found a median 9% loss of midface volume, mostly superficial, about 7% per 10 kg lost (D), and a survey of 1,226 patients found sagging, facial volume loss and hair shedding reported more often the more weight was lost (C). No randomized trial has measured the face. Regulatory status (US, September 2026): semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy) and tirzepatide (Mounjaro, Zepbound) are FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes, chronic weight management and further heart, liver and sleep-apnoea indications. Their labels list hair loss (about 3–6% on drug against about 1% on placebo, mostly in women, linked to weight reductio…

Mechanism: bacterial lipopolysaccharide crossing a leaky gut barrier ('metabolic endotoxaemia') drives inflammation and insulin resistance in mice, and a single high-fat meal briefly raised plasma endotoxin in a study of 12 healthy men (D). Human evidence for skin: an independent Cochrane review of 39 trials found probiotics probably make little or no difference to patient-rated eczema symptoms (B); a 2024 meta-analysis in children without food allergy reported small score improvements (C); one small randomized trial found rosacea improved after small-intestinal bacterial overgrowth was treated (C). A leading review concludes it is unproven that restoring barrier function improves disease outside the gut, and a widely used commercial zonulin assay detects proteins other than zonulin. A fibre-rich diet has strong evidence for cardiometabolic outcomes and has not been tested on skin outcom…

Topical GHK-Cu has a plausible copper-enzyme mechanism and small-trial human support (GRADE C); injected GHK-Cu has no randomized trials and commonly irritates. In the US, as of FDA's 14 May 2026 list, non-injectable GHK-Cu is in 503A Category 1 (under evaluation, not approved); the injectable route is excluded. In the UK, a GHK-Cu serum presented for appearance is regulated as a cosmetic, and cosmetics law excludes anything injected; MHRA decides from its claims, form and use whether an injected product is a medicine, and a medicine with no UK marketing authorisation may not be sold, supplied or advertised. This course gives no doses or sourcing advice — for an individual patient, that is the prescriber's decision.

BPC-157's evidence is rodent studies from one group plus uncontrolled case series; no randomized efficacy trial in people has been published in full (September 2026); the one randomized trial FDA found, in ulcerative colitis, exists only as a 2005 meeting abstract and showed no significant difference from placebo. TB-500 is a seven-residue fragment of thymosin beta-4 that has never been trialled; KPV has only mouse data. GLOW and KLOW are marketing names for untested blends. FDA's advisory committee reviewed BPC-157, KPV and TB-500 in July 2026 — advice only; they are not on the 503A bulks list. In the UK, a medicine with no marketing authorisation may not be sold, supplied or advertised, and MHRA's largest seizure of unlicensed weight-loss medicines, in May 2026, included peptide products. New pigmentation while using research-use-only peptides is a red flag: stop, record the product an…

Afamelanotide (Scenesse) is an MC1R agonist approved only for erythropoietic protoporphyria (EU 2014, US 2019; licensed in the UK, where NICE did not recommend it for NHS use in 2023), on the strength of two sponsor-funded phase 3 trials; even there, the US label recommends a full-body skin examination twice a year. Melanotan II is a different, non-selective molecule approved for no indication. Its only controlled human data are two tiny 1990s studies, and case reports describe darkening and new moles, nail pigmentation, melanomas in people with other risk factors (causation unproven), priapism and rhabdomyolysis. FDA (April 2026), MHRA (April 2024) and TGA (August 2026) have all put warnings on record. If someone has used it: stop, record the product and seller, examine the skin and nails, and refer changing moles; a personal or family history of melanoma makes it an absolute no in the …

PTD-DBM releases a brake (CXXC5) on Wnt signalling; its whole evidence is one 2017 mouse and tissue study from the developer's group, with no human trial published or registered as of September 2026 (grade D). Zinc thymulin is a zinc-dependent thymic peptide with no indexed human hair study (grade D). In the US, on FDA's 14 May 2026 lists, thymulin acetate is in 503A Category 3 and PTD-DBM is on no list; neither is on the bulks list. Hair loss starts with a workup (pattern, trigger, patches, androgens; ferritin and TSH in everyone), and the approved options, minoxidil, finasteride in men and baricitinib for severe alopecia areata, carry grade A evidence. In the UK, a men's minoxidil foam is on general sale, finasteride for hair loss is a private prescription carrying MHRA's strengthened warnings on depression and sexual dysfunction (May 2026), baricitinib is licensed for severe alopecia …

Tesamorelin is the one peptide on this axis with approval-grade evidence: two phase 3 trials and US approval (2010) for excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy, GRADE A for that use only. Sermorelin, CJC-1295 with DAC and ipamorelin have human hormone-level data but no trial showing a clinical or skin benefit; CJC-1295 without DAC and IGF-1 LR3 have no published human studies (this course grades all of these D). In the US, as of FDA's lists of April and May 2026, no growth-hormone secretagogue is on the 503A bulks list; ibutamoren (MK-677) is in Category 2, and the CJC-1295 and ipamorelin 503A nominations were withdrawn. Growth hormone itself is approved for diagnosed deficiency and a few growth disorders, and knowingly distributing it for anti-ageing is a federal offence in the US. Signs of growth-hormone excess include puffy, thickened skin of the face, hands and feet, oily skin, more sweating, skin tags, acanthosis nigricans, tight rings or shoes, night-time tingling and carpal tunnel symptoms. On GH-axis drugs, fluid retention with swelling and joint pain is common and usually settles when treatment stops. The Endocrine Society recommends IGF-1 testing when typical acral and facial features are present, so route these patients to a prescriber or to endocrinology. On cancer, keep four answers apart: the IGF-1 receptor drives cell growth (mechanism); higher natural IGF-1 goes with modestly higher risk of some cancers (observation); GH replacement in true deficiency has not shown a clear risk in large cohorts; and for secretagogues or IGF-1 LR3 used for skin, long-term cancer data do not exist (open question).

GRADE rates certainty for a specific outcome across a body of evidence: high, moderate, low or very low (the Hormonaly guides print A to D). Randomized trials start high; certainty drops for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision or suspected publication bias. Industry-sponsored studies more often report favourable results (Cochrane, 2017), so ask who ran and paid for the trials. A grade is separate from legal status: check both, and never let a mechanism raise a grade. This course gives no doses or sourcing advice.

In the US, a 503A pharmacy may compound only from a substance that meets a USP or NF monograph, or else is a component of an approved drug, or else is on the 503A bulks list (six substances, none a peptide, as of September 2026), and it needs a valid certificate of analysis. A certificate is the supplier's report on one lot: mass spectrometry for identity, HPLC for purity, plus endotoxin and microbial results. It cannot prove your vial is that lot, how it was stored, or that it is sterile or lawful. 'Research use only' products are labelled not for use in humans, and 'off-label' applies only to approved drugs.
